Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus-then-washout chromatin accessibility time course
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a transient AP-1-activating stimulus such as TPA, TNF, or wounding. After washout, run ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag for AP-1 (FOS/JUN), H3K27ac and H3K4me1 over days to weeks to see whether newly opened enhancers stay open after AP-1 binding has decayed.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation at different times after the stimulus
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged FOS, JUN or a dominant-negative (A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either during the stimulus or well after it. Measure whether accessibility and the faster secondary transcriptional response persist without continuing AP-1 activity. Persistence means the memory is independent of AP-1, and loss means AP-1 maintains it.

ideas.title: Functional re-stimulation assay of primed vs. naive cells
ideas.description: Give a first stimulus, rest the cells, then give a second stimulus. Compare nascent RNA (PRO-seq or SLAM-seq) and gene induction kinetics against naive cells. Repeat with AP-1 perturbed during only the priming phase to test whether AP-1 is necessary for the enhanced or faster response.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage-tracked memory persistence
ideas.description: Run paired scATAC and scRNA-seq with live reporters of AP-1 activity, using barcoded lineage tracing across cell divisions. This tests whether accessibility states are inherited clonally, whether memory is heterogeneous or bimodal, and whether it correlates with past AP-1 activity levels.

ideas.title: Targeted synthetic AP-1 site manipulation at memory loci
ideas.description: At candidate memory enhancers, use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs, or use dCas9-based recruitment or blocking of AP-1 and chromatin remodelers (e.g., BAF). Test whether the motif is needed to establish memory, to maintain it, or both. Read this out with allele-specific accessibility, histone marks and reporter induction after a delay. Add in vivo validation, such as epidermal stem cell wound memory in mice.
